statement: Let a string mean a finite sequence of bytes in the lowercase range 97..122. A string t is a subsequence of a string s if there are indices 0 <= p_0 < ... < p_{len(t)-1} < len(s) with s[p_k] = t[k]. A common supersequence of words is a string s such that every words[i] is a subsequence of s. Let M be the minimum length of a common supersequence (it exists, for example the concatenation of all words). An SCS is a common supersequence of length M. For any string s and any j with 0 <= j < 26, let F_s[j] be the number of indices p with 0 <= p < len(s) and s[p] = 97+j. The function returns a result r (it does not fail). The rows of r are exactly the set { F_s | s is an SCS }, with no repetitions: for every k with 0 <= k < len(r), r[k] = F_s for some SCS s; and for every SCS s there is exactly one k with r[k] = F_s. The order of the rows is unrestricted.
preconditions: words is a slice of byte vectors. Let n = len(words). 1 <= n <= 256. For every i with 0 <= i < n, len(words[i]) = 2, and for every j with 0 <= j < 2, 97 <= words[i][j] <= 122. For every i,k with 0 <= i < k < n, words[i] != words[k] as byte sequences. The set of bytes occurring in any word, { words[i][j] | 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < 2 }, has at most 16 elements.

statement: Let M be the least length of a common supersequence of words, where a common supersequence is a string over bytes 97..122 that contains each words[q] as a subsequence (there are indices 0 <= p_0 < ... < p_{len(words[q])-1} < len(s) with s[p_k] = words[q][k]). Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < len(r), sum_{j=0}^{25} r[i][j] = M.

(Each letter occurrence in a shortest common supersequence is needed by at least one word embedding, and a single word supplies at most C_j(words[q]) occurrences of letter j.)
preconditions: words is a slice of byte vectors with 1 <= n <= 256, each len(words[i]) = 2 with bytes in 97..122, words pairwise distinct, and at most 16 distinct bytes overall; C_j(w) = number of p with w[p] = 97+j.
